description: Four minds. One mission. Endless possibilities. We're a team of curious minds driven by innovation, creativity and a shared passion for solving real-world challenges. We believe the best ideas emerge when different perspectives come together, pushing boundaries and turning possibilities into meaningful solutions. With curiosity as our fuel and collaboration at our core, we're here to explore, experiment and build something that matters.
summary: ARGAL is an analogue finder that links places on the Moon and Mars to similar places on Earth. We built a curated database of sites: 10 lunar, 10 Martian and 15 Earth analogue locations, including Lake Salda in Turkey, the Atacama Desert in Chile and Hawaii’s lava tubes. Every site is described using the same six measures: surface temperature, atmospheric pressure, solar/UV flux, relief variance, regolith grain size and surface slope. A user picks a planetary site, such as Jezero Crater, and ARGAL compares it with the Earth sites, scores each match out of 100 and ranks them, with coordinates and a short geological description. Our top pairing is Jezero Crater and Lake Salda, at 89/100, because both involve ancient lake environments and carbonate deposits. This addresses the challenge by using open NASA data, including LRO, MGS and SRTM, to characterize Earth analogues in a consistent, comparable way. It matters because missions to the Moon and Mars are costly and hard to repeat, so teams must test rovers and habitats on Earth first. ARGAL gives them a clear starting shortlist, and it highlights fragile landscapes worth protecting. The similarity scores are platform-provided and no Earth site matches every condition, so ARGAL is a guide for choosing where to look closer, not a replacement for field testing.
details: ARGAL is an interactive web platform that helps people find places on Earth that resemble sites on the Moon and Mars. You explore the Moon, Mars or Earth on a 3D globe or a flat 2D map and pick a site, and a side panel shows its six physical characteristics: surface temperature, atmospheric pressure, solar/UV flux, relief, grain size and slope. ARGAL then compares that site with its catalogue of Earth locations and ranks them, combining terrain similarity (60%) with environmental similarity (40%), and lets you open any match for a detailed comparison that includes rover compatibility and field experiments. This saves researchers and students from piecing together scattered papers and maps, because every site is described the same way and comparison reports can be exported as Markdown. Our aim is to make planetary analogue exploration more accessible and visual, to point mission teams toward sensible places to test rovers and habitats before launch, and to highlight Earth landscapes, such as polar deserts, lava tubes and ancient lakebeds, that are worth studying and protecting. We built it with HTML5, CSS3 and JavaScript, using JavaScript for the 3D globes, Leaflet for the 2D maps, and NASA Trek and Esri map services for imagery . It is creative because it lets you travel across the Moon and Mars like a globe and see the Earth “twin” of any site, instead of reading a table of numbers. While designing it, we kept in mind that no Earth site can fully reproduce the Moon or Mars, so we treat the scores as a guide for deciding where to look closer, not as a replacement for field testing.
